title: Protection Against Second-hand Smoke in our Homes
what_it_is: Protection Against Second-hand Smoke in our Homes

sections.label: WHO second-hand smoke risks
sections.summary: The World Health Organization says there is no safe level of second-hand smoke exposure, which can cause coronary heart disease, stroke and lung cancer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The World Health Organization has said that there is no safe level of exposure to second-hand smoke, which can cause coronary heart disease, stroke and lung cancer.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke deaths Singapore
sections.summary: In 2016 alone, 383 people in Singapore died due to second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2016 alone, 383 people in Singapore died due to second-hand smoke.

sections.label: Smoking complaints and mediation cases
sections.summary: NEA received 11,400 smoking complaints in the first four months of this year, and CMC cigarette-smoke disputes quadrupled to eight cases a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the first four months of this year, NEA received 11,400 complaints related to smoking, a 20% increase from last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With more people working from home because of COVID-19, the number of cigarette-smoke disputes escalated to the Community Mediation Centre or CMC has quadrupled from two cases a month to now eight cases a month.

sections.label: Public housing smoking bans
sections.summary: The US and several provinces of Canada do not allow smoking in public housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The US, as well as several provinces of Canada, does not allow smoking in public housing.

sections.label: Foresque Residences smoking restriction vote
sections.summary: Foresque Residences in Singapore implemented the restriction itself, with 84.4% of residents voting in favour last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One condominium in Singapore, Foresque Residences, has already implemented this restriction on their own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, an overwhelming 84.4% of residents voted in favour of it.

sections.label: Cameras and enforcement actions
sections.summary: Cameras can capture cigarette butts thrown from windows, helping raise successful enforcement actions from 10 in 2011 to over 1,200 in 2018, and NEA uses thermal surveillance cameras.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It can even capture someone throwing cigarette butts out of their window.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These cameras have contributed to hugely increasing a number of successful enforcement actions from 10 in 2011 to over 1,200 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Separately, NEA has also been using thermal surveillance cameras to catch residents smoking at prohibited areas, such as common corridors, lift lobbies and staircase landings.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke near windows
sections.summary: Second-hand smoke near windows and balconies kills people and should be acted on with the same urgency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second-hand smoke near windows and balconies also kills people and we should act on it with the same urgency.

sections.label: Smoking prohibited in 32,000 places
sections.summary: Smoking is currently prohibited in more than 32,000 places and more will be done.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Currently, smoking is prohibited in more than 32,000 places and we will do more.

sections.label: Smoking prevalence and complaints
sections.summary: Daily smoking prevalence fell from 18.3% in 1992 to 10.6% in 2019, and 58% of 11,400 complaints in early 2020 were in residential estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Consequently, the daily smoking prevalence has decreased from 18.3% in 1992 to 13.9% in 2010 and 10.6% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Of the 11,400 smoking complaints received in the first four months of 2020, 58% or 6,630 complaints were in residential estates.

sections.label: NEA enforcement actions increase
sections.summary: In the first half of 2020, NEA took 2,400 enforcement actions at these areas, a 37% increase from the same period last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2020, NEA took 2,400 enforcement actions at these areas, a 37% increase from the same time period last year.

sections.label: CDRT excessive smoke claims
sections.summary: Between January 2019 and July 2020, 25 claims relating to excessive smoke from cigarettes or incense were filed with the CDRT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Between January 2019 and July 2020, 25 claims relating to excessive smoke, caused by cigarettes or incense, were filed with the CDRT.

sections.label: Enforcement challenging, legislation not silver bullet
sections.summary: Overseas examples show enforcement is challenging, and legislation against smoking at windows or balconies may not be that silver bullet.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The overseas examples show that enforcement is challenging.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We must work hard to address the difficult issue of second-hand smoke from homes but legislation against smoking at windows or balconies may not be that silver bullet.

sections.label: Facilitating neighbour conversations
sections.summary: The government will examine more ways to facilitate productive conversations between neighbours before situations escalate into intractable disputes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Second, we will examine more ways to facilitate productive conversations between neighbours to deal with difficult situations, before they escalate into intractable disputes.

sections.label: Community dispute management review
sections.summary: Agencies will study how disputes can be better addressed by the Community Dispute Management Framework and review the Community Mediation Process and CDRT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Third, we will work with agencies to study how these disputes can be better addressed by the inter-agency Community Dispute Management Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will work with agencies to review the Community Mediation Process and the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal or CDRT to enhance their effectiveness when residents have to resort to these channels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The best way to protect against second-hand smoke is for family members and neighbours to help smokers cut down and quit smoking.

sections.label: Smoking ban in common areas
sections.summary: Legislation to ban smoking in common areas aims to protect the public from second-hand smoke, with 32,000 smoking prohibited places now.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The fact that we started legislation to ban smoking in common areas, really, one of the priority is because we want to protect the public from second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: That is why there are 32,000 places now that are smoking prohibited areas.

sections.label: Smoking prevalence and prohibited areas
sections.summary: The reason is protecting the public from second-hand smoke and making smoking difficult, and smoking prevalence fell to 10.6% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The reason really is protecting public from second-hand smoke as well as of course making it very difficult for smokers to smoke because we hope that that will help to reduce their smoking prevalence rate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And indeed, we have been successful in doing this because I have actually given statistics to show that smoking prevalence rates have fallen to 10.6% in 2019, and we are doing more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We are going to expand the smoking prohibited areas to even more places.

sections.label: Thermal camera range
sections.summary: Thermal cameras have a shorter range than optical cameras for high-rise littering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: First of all, thermal cameras are of shorter range than the optical cameras for high-rise littering.

sections.label: Thermal camera distance limits
sections.summary: Thermal cameras have a distance of only 40 metres, so trees or blockage prevent getting the heat signature.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: For thermal cameras, the distance is only 40 metres so you can well imagine if you are separated or blocked by trees, so on and so forth, you will not be able to get the heat signature.
